abating.ex: The storm showed no sign of abating by midnight.

example.en: The rain finally abated in the evening.

note.usage: 多用於風暴、疫情、需求等；常見 show no sign of abating。

noteEn.usage: Common phrase: 'show no sign of abating'.

noteEs.exampleTr: La lluvia por fin amainó por la tarde.
noteEs.usage: Para tormentas o demanda; show no sign of abating.

noteHi.exampleTr: शाम को बारिश आख़िरकार कम हुई।
noteHi.usage: तूफ़ान, माँग आदि के लिए; show no sign of abating।

noteJa.exampleTr: 夕方になってようやく雨が弱まった。
noteJa.usage: 嵐・需要などに使う；show no sign of abating が定番。

noteKo.usage: 폭풍, 수요 등에 쓴다; show no sign of abating.

about.ex: The trip takes about an hour.

according.ex: According to the report, prices fell last year.

accounts.ex: The accounts show a small profit this year.
accounts.zh: 帳目（Public Accounts Committee：公共帳目委員會）

acknowledged.ex: He acknowledged that the plan had problems.

activity.en: something people do, often for fun
activity.ex: Swimming is my favourite weekend activity.

added.en: added up to: reached a total of
added.ex: The small costs added up to a lot.

addition.en: in addition to: as well as
addition.ex: In addition to French, she speaks Italian.

administrative.ex: The job includes a lot of administrative work.

adrift.ex: The team is six points adrift of the leaders.

agencies.ex: Hospitals use agencies to find extra nurses.

agency.en: an organisation that provides a service
agency.ex: A government agency manages the national parks.

allocated.ex: The council allocated money for new parks.

allocation.ex: The school's allocation was cut this year.

allowed.ex: The teacher allowed us to leave early.

almost.ex: The train was almost empty at midnight.

amounted.ex: The bill amounted to nearly 200 euro.

annual.en: every year (annual leave: holiday from work)
annual.ex: Workers get twenty days of annual leave.

approximately.ex: The journey takes approximately two hours.

around.ex: Around fifty people came to the meeting.

as.en: in the same way; in the role of

asks.ex: Mum asks me to tidy my room every day.

at.es: a (at the same rate: al mismo ritmo)
at.hi: पर (at the same rate: उसी दर पर)
at.ja: 〜で（at the same rate：同じ割合で）
at.zh: 以（at the same rate：以相同速度）

attendances.en: the number of visits by people
attendances.ex: Cinema attendances rose during the holidays.

attributable.ex: The fall in sales is attributable to bad weather.

example.en: Most of the delays were attributable to bad weather.
example.zh: 大部分延誤都是惡劣天氣造成的。

note.usage: 固定搭配 be attributable to + 名詞，用於正式說明原因。

noteEn.usage: Use 'be attributable to' + noun, mostly in formal writing.

noteEs.exampleTr: La mayoría de los retrasos se debieron al mal tiempo.
noteEs.usage: Se usa en la estructura 'be attributable to + sustantivo', en registro formal.

noteHi.exampleTr: अधिकांश देरी ख़राब मौसम के कारण हुई।
noteHi.usage: हमेशा 'attributable to + संज्ञा' के रूप में; औपचारिक भाषा में।

noteJa.exampleTr: 遅れのほとんどは悪天候が原因だった。
noteJa.usage: be attributable to + 名詞 の形で、改まった文で原因を述べる。

noteKo.usage: be attributable to + 명사 형태로 격식 있게 원인을 말할 때 쓴다.

august.en: the eighth month of the year

back.en: to where it was before (pay back)
back.ex: Please pay the money back by Friday.

bare.en: lay bare: show clearly something hidden
bare.ex: The report laid bare the problems in the system.

barred.en: officially not allowed to do or have something
barred.ex: He was barred from the club for fighting.

be.ex: Try to be on time tomorrow.

beds.en: places for patients in a hospital

been.ex: It has been a busy week.

behind.ex: The builders are two weeks behind.

being.ex: The main idea being simple, everyone understood.

belated.en: done later than it should be
belated.ex: He sent a belated birthday card to his aunt.

between.en: in the space or time separating two things

billion.ex: The project cost two billion euro.

budget.en: a plan for how much money to spend
budget.ex: We went over our holiday budget.

busy.ex: The city centre is very busy on Saturdays.

came.en: came to: reached a total of

cancer.en: a serious disease where cells grow wrongly
cancer.ex: Early tests help doctors find cancer sooner.

cannot.ex: You cannot park here after six.

capacity.en: the amount something can hold or supply
capacity.ex: The stadium has a capacity of 50,000 people.

cent.ex: Prices rose by five per cent.

checks.ex: She checks her email every morning.

clerical.ex: A clerical error put the wrong date on my bill.

climb.ex: Prices may climb again next year.

clinics.ex: The new clinic opens every morning at eight.

come.ex: Most of our food comes from abroad.

committee.en: a group chosen to do a task
committee.ex: The committee will decide next week.

companies.en: businesses that make or sell things
companies.ex: Many companies let staff work from home.

compared.ex: Prices are low compared with last year.

compiled.ex: She compiled a list of useful websites.

compounding.ex: Bad weather is compounding the delays.

example.zh: 交通擁擠使延誤更加嚴重。

note.usage: compound a problem = 使問題更糟；Compounding the problem, ... 常置句首。

noteEn.usage: 'Compounding the problem, ...' often starts a sentence.

noteEs.exampleTr: El tráfico intenso agravó los retrasos.
noteEs.usage: compound a problem = empeorarlo; a menudo al inicio de la frase.

noteHi.exampleTr: भारी ट्रैफ़िक ने देरी और बढ़ा दी।
noteHi.usage: compound a problem = समस्या और बिगाड़ना।

noteJa.exampleTr: 激しい渋滞が遅れをさらに悪化させた。
noteJa.usage: compound a problem の形；文頭で Compounding the problem, とも言う。

noteKo.exampleTr: 극심한 교통 체증이 지연을 더 악화시켰다.
noteKo.usage: compound a problem 형태; 문두에 자주 쓴다.

comprising.ex: A team comprising five players won.

concern.ex: There is growing concern about rents.

consequence.ex: He lost his job as a consequence of the accident.
consequence.zh: as a consequence of：由於…的結果

consequently.ex: It rained heavily; consequently, the match was cancelled.

example.en: He missed the bus and consequently arrived late.
example.zh: 他錯過了公車，因此遲到了。

note.usage: 連接副詞，多放句首並加逗號，用於正式寫作表示因果。

noteEn.usage: Often at the start of a sentence, followed by a comma.

noteEs.exampleTr: Perdió el autobús y, en consecuencia, llegó tarde.
noteEs.usage: Suele ir al inicio de la frase con coma; registro formal.

noteHi.exampleTr: उसकी बस छूट गई और परिणामस्वरूप वह देर से पहुँचा।
noteHi.usage: औपचारिक लेखन में वाक्य की शुरुआत में अल्पविराम के साथ।

noteJa.exampleTr: 彼はバスに乗り遅れ、その結果遅刻した。
noteJa.usage: 文頭でコンマとともに使うことが多い。フォーマルな書き言葉。

noteKo.exampleTr: 그는 버스를 놓쳐서 결과적으로 늦게 도착했다.
noteKo.usage: 주로 문장 앞에 쉼표와 함께 쓰며 격식 있는 글에 쓴다.

consultant.ex: The consultant explained the results of my scan.

consultants.en: senior hospital doctors who are specialists
consultants.ex: Two consultants checked the patient this morning.

contingent.ex: The deal is contingent on government funding.

example.en: The job offer is contingent on a health check.
example.zh: 這份工作錄取要以通過健康檢查為條件。

note.meaning: 取決於某條件；要等某事發生才成立。
note.usage: 固定搭配 contingent on/upon + 名詞，語氣正式，常見於合約與政策。

noteEn.meaning: depending on something else happening first.
noteEn.usage: Use 'contingent on' or 'contingent upon' + noun; it is formal.

noteEs.exampleTr: La oferta de trabajo depende de un examen médico.
noteEs.usage: Se usa contingent on/upon + sustantivo; es formal.

noteHi.exampleTr: नौकरी का प्रस्ताव स्वास्थ्य जाँच पर निर्भर है।
noteHi.usage: contingent on/upon + संज्ञा; औपचारिक प्रयोग, अनुबंधों में आम।

noteJa.exampleTr: その採用は健康診断が条件となっている。
noteJa.usage: contingent on/upon＋名詞 の形で使う。改まった表現。

noteKo.exampleTr: 그 일자리 제안은 건강 검진 통과가 조건이다.
noteKo.usage: contingent on/upon + 명사 형태로 쓰며 격식체이다.

contract.en: a legal written agreement about work
contract.ex: He signed a two-year contract with the club.

controls.en: rules or checks that limit something
controls.ex: Better controls could stop the mistakes.

conversely.ex: Some like the plan; conversely, others hate it.

example.en: Cheap loans boost spending; conversely, high rates slow it.
example.zh: 低息貸款刺激消費；相反地，高利率會抑制消費。

note.usage: 常置句首加逗號，用來引出與前句相反的情況。

noteEn.usage: Often starts a sentence with a comma to give the opposite case.

noteEs.exampleTr: Los préstamos baratos impulsan el gasto; por el contrario, los tipos altos lo frenan.
noteEs.meaning: De forma opuesta; por el contrario.
noteEs.usage: Suele ir al inicio con coma para presentar la situación opuesta.

noteHi.exampleTr: सस्ते ऋण खर्च बढ़ाते हैं; इसके विपरीत, ऊँची दरें उसे धीमा करती हैं।
noteHi.usage: प्रायः वाक्य के आरंभ में अल्पविराम के साथ, उल्टी स्थिति बताने के लिए।

noteJa.exampleTr: 低金利の融資は消費を促し、逆に高金利は消費を抑える。
noteJa.usage: 文頭でカンマとともに使い、前文と逆の状況を示す。

noteKo.exampleTr: 저금리 대출은 소비를 늘리고, 반대로 고금리는 소비를 줄인다.
noteKo.usage: 보통 문장 앞에 쉼표와 함께 써서 반대 상황을 제시.

cost.en: to need an amount of money; price

costs.ex: The cost of living keeps rising.

cover.en: people doing a job for a short time
cover.ex: The school found cover for the sick teacher.

data.en: facts and numbers collected for study
data.ex: The app collects data about your sleep.

dated.en: having a certain date written on it

december.en: the twelfth month of the year

decline.ex: There is a decline in sales.

deficit.en: money spent above what you have
deficit.ex: The company has a large deficit.

example.en: The country faces a deficit of qualified nurses.
example.zh: 這個國家面臨合格護理師短缺的問題。

note.meaning: 不足、缺口；本文指語言能力上的落後差距（也可指財政赤字）。
note.usage: 常用 a deficit in/of + 名詞；address/reduce a deficit 表示處理缺口。

noteEn.meaning: A lack or shortage of something needed.
noteEn.usage: Say 'a deficit in/of' something; also used for money.

noteEs.exampleTr: El país sufre un déficit de enfermeras cualificadas.
noteEs.meaning: Falta o carencia; aquí, el retraso en idiomas (también déficit económico).
noteEs.usage: Se usa a deficit in/of + sustantivo; address a deficit es afrontarlo.

noteHi.exampleTr: देश योग्य नर्सों की कमी का सामना कर रहा है।
noteHi.meaning: किसी चीज़ की कमी; यहाँ भाषा कौशल में कमी (वित्तीय घाटा भी हो सकता है)।
noteHi.usage: a deficit in/of + संज्ञा के साथ आता है; address a deficit यानी कमी दूर करना।

noteJa.exampleTr: その国は有資格の看護師不足に直面している。
noteJa.meaning: 不足や欠如。本文では語学力の遅れ（財政赤字の意味もある）。
noteJa.usage: a deficit in/of + 名詞 の形。address a deficit で「不足に対処する」。

noteKo.exampleTr: 그 나라는 자격 있는 간호사 부족 문제에 직면해 있다.
noteKo.meaning: 부족이나 결핍. 본문에서는 언어 능력의 격차(재정 적자의 뜻도 있음).
noteKo.usage: a deficit in/of + 명사 형태로 쓰며, address a deficit는 부족을 해결한다는 뜻.

demand.en: the need or wish for goods or services
demand.ex: There is high demand for new homes.

department.ex: The Department of Health published a report.

departments.ex: She works in the emergency department.

directly.ex: The bank is directly opposite the station.

document.en: an official written paper or report
document.ex: Please sign the document at the bottom.

double.ex: Prices are almost double what they were.

drop.ex: There was a drop in prices.

during.en: at some time in a period

dáil's.en: belonging to Ireland's lower house of parliament

earmarked.ex: The money is earmarked for new schools.

earning.ex: She is earning more in her new job.

employee.en: a person who works for a company
employee.ex: Each employee gets 20 days of holiday.

end.ex: We left at the end of the film.

entry.ex: Data entry takes most of her day.

euro.ex: A coffee costs about three euro.

executive.ex: The health executive runs the hospitals.

expected.ex: We expect the results on Monday.

example.en: Government expenditure on education rose by 5%.

note.usage: 多用於政府或機構的支出；expenditure on + 名詞；比 spending 正式。

noteEn.meaning: money spent, especially by an organisation.
noteEn.usage: 'expenditure on X' — formal, good for IELTS Task 1.

noteEs.exampleTr: El gasto público en educación subió un 5%.
noteEs.usage: expenditure on + sustantivo; más formal que spending.

noteHi.usage: expenditure on + संज्ञा; spending से औपचारिक।

noteJa.exampleTr: 教育への政府支出は5%増えた。
noteJa.usage: expenditure on＋名詞。spendingより改まった語。

extra.ex: The job comes with extra holidays.

far.ex: This phone is far better than my old one.

fear.ex: Locals fear the area will change too much.

fee-paying.ex: Fee-paying schools can be very expensive.

fees.ex: School fees went up this year.

figure.ex: The official figure is much higher.

filled.en: made full; given to someone (a job)
filled.ex: All the seats were filled within minutes.

first.ex: It was her first trip to Ireland.

found.ex: It is hard to find a cheap flat.

freedom.en: freedom (Freedom of Information: right to see official records)
freedom.ex: Freedom of speech is important in a democracy.
freedom.zh: 自由（Freedom of Information：資訊公開）

gap.ex: There is a gap in the budget.

given.ex: Given the rain, we stayed inside.

government.en: the group that runs a country

grew.ex: The company grew quickly last year.

group.en: a number of people or things together
group.ex: A group of students visited the museum.

grow.en: to get bigger; to live as a plant
grow.ex: Ireland grows a lot of potatoes.

had.ex: She had a small shop in the town.

has.en: owns or holds; also forms perfect tense

have.ja: 持つ；〜しなければならない

health.ex: The health service is under pressure.

hit.en: to strike badly; to reach (a level)
hit.ex: Prices could hit a new record this year.

hospitals.en: places where sick people are treated
hospitals.ex: Hospitals are very busy in winter.

however.ex: It was sunny; however, it was cold.

hse.ja: HSE（アイルランド保健サービス庁）
hse.zh: HSE 愛爾蘭衛生服務管理局

implies.ex: His silence implies that he agrees.

improved.ex: The improved service is faster and cheaper.

income.ex: Rent takes half of her income.

increase.ex: There was a sharp increase in prices.

indicate.en: to show or be a sign of

indicates.ex: The test indicates that the water is safe.

inefficiencies.en: ways of wasting time or money
inefficiencies.ex: The new software cut many inefficiencies.

information.ex: The website has useful information for travellers.

informed.ex: The teacher informed us about the test.

internal.ex: The company held an internal meeting about pay.

january.en: the first month of the year

just.ex: Just over half the class passed.

last.ex: The last agreement ended in June.

late.ex: The train was late again this morning.

lays.ex: The film lays bare the life of farm workers.

leaving.ex: She is on annual leave this week.

less.ex: I spend less on food now.

linked.ex: Poor sleep is linked to stress.

longer.ex: The talks were long and difficult.

lucrative.ex: She left a lucrative job to start a charity.

example.en: She turned down a lucrative offer from a bank.
example.zh: 她拒絕了一家銀行的高薪邀約。

note.usage: 多修飾 contract, job, market, deal；比 profitable 更強調「錢多」。

noteEn.meaning: bringing in a lot of money.

noteEs.exampleTr: Rechazó una oferta lucrativa de un banco.
noteEs.usage: Se usa con contract, job, market, deal.

noteHi.exampleTr: उसने एक बैंक का लाभदायक प्रस्ताव ठुकरा दिया।
noteHi.usage: contract, job, market के साथ आता है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 彼女は銀行からの高収入の申し出を断った。
noteJa.usage: contract, job, market などと結びつく。

noteKo.usage: contract, job, market 등과 함께 쓴다.

may.ex: Kids may start school at four.
may.ja: …かもしれない；…することがある

million.ex: The city has over one million people.

mistake.ex: I made a mistake in my phone number.

money.ex: They saved money for a new car.

mounting.ex: There is mounting pressure on hospitals.

much.ex: The new phone is much faster.

nevertheless.ex: It was raining; nevertheless, we went out.

new.ex: The city opened a new library.

no.ex: She said no to the offer.

non-pay.ex: Non-pay costs include drugs and equipment.

normal.ja: 通常の（as normal：通常どおり）

now.ex: The shop is now open on Sundays.

nursing.en: having to deal with a problem
nursing.ex: The club is nursing large debts after the season.

obtained.ex: He obtained a visa to work abroad.

organisation.ex: She works for a charity organisation.

out.en: away; finished (phasing out, the year is out)
out.ex: The milk will be out of date soon.
out.zh: （phasing out：逐步淘汰；the year is out：年底前）

outside.en: not from or part of something

overall.ex: The overall cost was higher than planned.

overpaid.ex: The company overpaid him by mistake.

overrun.ex: The project had a cost overrun of 10 per cent.

overshot.ex: The project overshot its budget by a third.

oversight.en: the job of checking that things are done properly
oversight.ex: An oversight group checks the spending.

overspend.ex: Try not to overspend at Christmas.

overspent.ex: The council overspent on the new bridge.

overtime.ex: Nurses work a lot of overtime.

paradoxically.ex: Paradoxically, the cheaper plan cost more in the end.

past.en: the time before now (in the past)
past.ex: In the past, people wrote letters.

patients.ex: The nurse looked after ten patients.

payroll.en: the list and system for paying workers
payroll.ex: The payroll team pays staff each month.

per.ex: The ticket costs ten euro per person.

period.ex: The museum is closed for a short period.

permanent.en: lasting for a long time or always
permanent.ex: The museum has a permanent home at last.

personnel.en: the people employed in an organisation
personnel.ex: All hospital personnel must wear name cards.

phasing.en: phasing out: ending slowly in steps
phasing.ex: The phasing out of coal took ten years.

plugged.ex: The leak was plugged within an hour.

practice.ex: She opened a private practice in Cork.

predominantly.ex: The town is predominantly young families.

note.usage: 修飾形容詞或介系詞片語；比 mainly 正式，適合 IELTS 寫作描述數據。

noteEn.usage: A formal alternative to 'mainly', useful in IELTS Task 1.

noteEs.usage: Más formal que mainly; útil para describir datos.

noteHi.exampleTr: कार्यबल मुख्य रूप से युवा है।
noteHi.usage: mainly से अधिक औपचारिक; आँकड़ों के वर्णन में उपयोगी।

noteJa.usage: mainlyより改まった語。データ描写に便利。

primarily.ex: The course is primarily for adults.

private.en: paid for by people, not the government
private.ex: She works for a private company.

produced.ex: The team produced a short video.

productivity.en: how much work is done for the cost
productivity.ex: New tools raised productivity by 20 per cent.

prohibited.ex: Smoking is prohibited in the building.

projections.ex: Population projections show the city will grow.

public.ex: Public transport is cheap in the city.

public-only.en: allowing only public, not private, work
public-only.ex: He signed a public-only contract last year.

reach.ex: Sales could reach two million this year.

reason.ex: There is no reason to worry.

recorded.ex: This was the wettest month on record.

records.ex: Keep your medical records in a safe place.

recourse.en: something you can use or turn to for help
recourse.ex: Without savings, they had no recourse but to borrow.

recruit.ex: Hospitals are trying to recruit nurses.

reforms.ex: The government promised major tax reforms.

represents.ex: This result represents a big improvement.

result.en: what happens because of something (as a result)
result.ex: As a result, the road was closed.

reveal.ex: The figures reveal a rise in sales.

revealed.ex: The report revealed a big drop in sales.

running.ex: The club is running at a loss.
running.zh: 處於（running a deficit：出現赤字）；運作

runs.ex: Her family runs a small hotel.

saw.ex: The shop saw more customers in December.

says.ex: Experts say the plan will work.

separate.ex: They did a separate test on the water.

separately.en: in a different report or way
separately.ex: Separately, police reported a fall in burglaries.

service.ex: The bus service runs every hour.

services.ex: The bus service runs every hour.

shortfall.ex: There is a shortfall in funding.

example.en: The school faces a shortfall of five teachers.
example.zh: 這所學校面臨五名教師的短缺。

note.meaning: 實際金額或數量低於所需的差額；缺口。
note.usage: 常用 a shortfall of + 數額 / a shortfall in + 名詞，多見於財經報導。

noteEn.meaning: the amount by which something is less than needed.
noteEn.usage: Use 'a shortfall of' + amount or 'a shortfall in' + noun.

noteEs.exampleTr: La escuela tiene un déficit de cinco profesores.
noteEs.meaning: cantidad que falta para llegar a lo necesario; déficit.
noteEs.usage: Se usa a shortfall of + cifra o a shortfall in + sustantivo.

noteHi.exampleTr: स्कूल में पाँच शिक्षकों की कमी है।
noteHi.meaning: ज़रूरत से कम राशि या संख्या; कमी।

paragraphs: Ireland's health service is spending too much money. A new report from the HSE shows this. The HSE runs public hospitals in Ireland.

The HSE planned to spend 272 million euro on agency staff. Agency workers are not full staff. They come from outside companies. By the end of August, it spent 522 million euro. That is about 250 million euro more than planned. Agency workers can cost 40 per cent more than normal staff.
The HSE is now short of about 660 million euro. Some people in the Government think this could reach one billion euro by December.
Hospitals are also very busy. More than 1.1 million people went to emergency departments this year. That is 7 per cent more than last year.
Another report shows the HSE paid some staff too much by mistake. Over three years, this came to more than 30 million euro.

Ireland's health service, the HSE, has spent far more money than planned on workers from staffing agencies, according to an internal report. By the end of August, it had spent 522 million euro on agency staff. Its budget for that period was only 272 million euro, so it went over by about 250 million euro.

The report was written by a HSE group that checks costs and productivity. It also found that the HSE spent about 52 million euro more than planned on overtime. However, it spent about 220 million euro less than expected on its own directly employed staff. In September, the HSE told politicians that an agency worker can cost around 40 per cent more than a normal employee.

Overall, the HSE had a gap of almost 660 million euro between its spending and its budget by the end of August. Some people in the Government are worried that this gap could reach one billion euro by the end of the year.

One reason is that the HSE is earning less money. Since January, consultants on new public-only contracts cannot treat private patients in public hospitals. In the past, these patients paid fees. Income from private patients is now 99 million euro lower than planned.

Demand is also rising. More than 1.1 million people went to emergency departments by August, 7.2 per cent more than last year. Hospitals used extra beds much more often, and cancer clinics saw more patients than expected.

In a separate report, the HSE said it had paid staff too much by mistake. Between 2023 and 2025, these overpayments added up to more than 30 million euro. The HSE says it asks workers to pay the money back.

The Health Service Executive (HSE) overspent its budget for agency staff by more than 250 million euro in the first eight months of the year, an internal report has revealed. By the end of August, the health service had spent 522 million euro on agency workers, against a budget of 272 million euro for the period.

The figures come from a report by the HSE's cost and productivity oversight group, dated 25 September. It also shows that overtime costs were around 52 million euro above budget, while spending on directly employed staff was about 220 million euro below the 7.29 billion euro allocated. The HSE recently told the Dáil's Public Accounts Committee that an agency worker can cost roughly 40 per cent more than a directly recruited employee.

In total, the HSE was running a deficit of just under 660 million euro at the end of August. This included a pay overspend of 172.5 million euro, a non-pay deficit of 423.6 million euro and an income shortfall of 63.2 million euro. There are concerns within Government that the full-year deficit could hit one billion euro.

The drop in income is linked to the Sláintecare reforms. Since the start of this year, consultants on the public-only contract are no longer allowed to treat fee-paying patients in public hospitals. As a result, private consultant income is 99 million euro, or 44 per cent, behind budget.

At the same time, demand continues to grow. Emergency department attendances passed 1.1 million, up 7.2 per cent on last year, and the use of surge beds rose by 44 per cent. Cancer clinics also exceeded their activity targets.

Separately, figures released under Freedom of Information show the HSE overpaid staff by more than 30 million euro between 2023 and 2025, often because of data entry errors and late updates to payroll.

The Health Service Executive has overshot its budget for agency staff by upwards of 250 million euro in just eight months, according to an internal report that lays bare the mounting strain on the State's health finances. Outlays on agency workers had reached 522 million euro by the end of August, almost double the 272 million euro earmarked for the period.

Compiled by the HSE's cost and productivity oversight group and dated 25 September, the report also shows overtime running some 52 million euro over budget. Paradoxically, spending on directly employed staff was roughly 220 million euro below its 7.29 billion euro allocation, suggesting that vacancies are being plugged with pricier temporary cover. The executive has acknowledged to the Public Accounts Committee that an agency worker can cost about 40 per cent more than a permanent recruit.

Taken together, the HSE was nursing a deficit of just under 660 million euro, comprising a 172.5 million euro pay overrun, a 423.6 million euro non-pay shortfall and a 63.2 million euro gap in income. Government sources fear the year-end figure could climb to one billion euro.

The income gap stems largely from the Sláintecare-driven phasing out of private practice in public hospitals. Consultants who signed the lucrative public-only contract have been barred from treating fee-paying patients since January, leaving private consultant income 99 million euro, or 44 per cent, adrift of target.

Meanwhile, demand shows no sign of abating. Emergency department attendances topped 1.1 million, a 7.2 per cent year-on-year rise, while recourse to surge beds soared by 44 per cent and cancer clinics outstripped their targets.

Compounding the picture, records released under Freedom of Information reveal that the HSE overpaid staff by more than 30 million euro between 2023 and 2025, largely owing to clerical errors and belated payroll updates.
